clue.text: Send stopwatch back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the stopwatch's synonym from right to left

parts.note: a stopwatch is a timer

explanation.surface: An order to return a stopwatch to its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit money or papers is to dispatch them to someone, a synonym of send.

clue.text: Sorry about code nearly complete

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Morse is the famous dot-and-dash telegraph code

indicators.note: nearly says the word for complete loses its final letter

parts.note: full means complete

explanation.surface: An apology for a code that is not quite finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts the last L from FULL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sorry for a wrong feels regret, which is what remorseful describes.

clue.text: Doctors go with our leader to find spreader of disease

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, so MOS is doctors
to quit is to go or leave

indicators.note: our leader means the opening letter of the word our

explanation.surface: Medics leave with their chief to track down the carrier of an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosquitoes carry malaria and other illnesses between people, so the insect is a disease vector.

clue.text: Peg's reportedly damaged item of clothing

parts.note: a tee is a golf peg, so peg's is tee's

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase built from the words around it is spoken, matching a word spelt differently

parts.note: hurt means damaged

explanation.surface: Someone called Peg is said to have damaged a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg' looks like a woman's name; it is a golf tee. Said out loud, 'tee's hurt' is the garment, so the HURT sound is written HIRT after the S of TEES.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved casual top is a common garment.

clue.text: Coat underneath border

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
below means underneath

explanation.surface: A coat worn under a trimmed edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a flounce or ruffled trim along the hem of a garment, a decorative border.

clue.text: Most of the ships escape

indicators.note: most of says the word for the ships loses its last letter

parts.note: a fleet is a body of ships

explanation.surface: Most of a navy's vessels get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the final T of FLEET.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, a synonym of escape.

clue.text: Carrier sounds as if he is not wearing so many clothes

indicators.note: sounds as if says the word meant by the following phrase is heard, not seen

parts.words: he is not wearing so many clothes
parts.note: someone wearing fewer clothes is barer

explanation.surface: A porter who seems to be wearing less than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearer carries something, a stretcher or a coffin, so is a carrier.

clue.text: Plate beast upended

indicators.note: upended in a down clue means the word for beast is turned bottom to top

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A dish with an animal flipped over on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamina is a thin plate or layer of material, as in laminated.

clue.text: Markedly wrong during established routine to be covered with sticky substance

indicators.note: during says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: way means an established routine, as in set in one's ways
X is the mark a teacher puts by a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A muddled sentence about getting gummed up in daily habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts X, the mark for wrong, inside WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxy describes something coated with wax, a soft clinging substance.

clue.text: She causes friction when she is at work

definitions.text: She causes friction when she is at work

parts.words: She causes friction when she is at work
parts.note: friction sounds like workplace trouble, but here it is literal rubbing: a woman whose job is to rub people down

explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages rubs the body, producing friction as her trade.

clue.text: A ring that goes on for ever

definitions.meaning: a band with stones set all the way round, given as a token of lasting love

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery said to last without end.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternity ring has gems set unbroken all round; the word itself means endless time.

clue.text: Match-box that creates a precedent?

parts.note: a test is a cricket match, a Test match
a case is a box

explanation.surface: A matchbox that starts a new fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match-box' looks like one object; split it into match (Test) and box (case).
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose ruling sets a precedent for later ones.

clue.text: Violently and in a crude way

explanation.surface: Two ways of doing something without finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a lack of care: done with force, or done approximately without refinement.

clue.text: Most youthful guy on set elaborated

indicators.note: elaborated means worked out in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fellow on a film set embellishing his story.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of young names the person of least age in a group.

clue.text: Perceptive old boy attendant

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a servant is an attendant

explanation.surface: A former pupil who works as a sharp-eyed footman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone perceptive notices things quickly, which is being observant.

clue.text: Across which one must pay one's way

definitions.text: Across which one must pay one's way

parts.words: Across which one must pay one's way
parts.note: paying one's way sounds like meeting one's expenses, but here it is a literal fee to cross a span

explanation.definitionFit: A bridge charging a fee to motorists or walkers who cross it.

clue.text: Money for HMS Belfast?

definitions.meaning: funds held in a fluid form available for use
the warship moored as a museum on the Thames, afloat in London

explanation.surface: Asking what cash is needed for a famous warship.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Belfast is a Second World War cruiser permanently moored in London, the UK capital, as a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Circulating funds not tied up in fixed assets are floating capital; the ship literally floats in the capital city.

clue.text: Lavish gold pair removed

indicators.note: removed read as re-moved, shifted about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Extravagant jewellery: a gold pair taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, spending freely as in the parable's son.

clue.text: It's a sin to intrude on another's land

definitions.meaning: as in forgive us our ..., a wrongdoing
to enter private property without permission

explanation.surface: A moral pronouncement about entering someone else's property.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a moral wrong in the Lord's Prayer and unlawful entry onto property.

clue.text: Lower boundary first has no restrictions

indicators.note: first says the boundary word comes before the other piece

parts.note: a limit is a boundary
less means lower in amount

explanation.surface: A rule that dropping the edge first removes all constraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts LIMIT ahead of LESS though the clue names them the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without bounds or curbs is unbounded, which is what limitless says.

clue.text: Ram hat crookedly on Mary's sister

indicators.note: crookedly means set askew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone puts a hat askew on a biblical woman's sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels Martha and Mary of Bethany are sisters of Lazarus.

clue.text: Arrive upset

definitions.meaning: a ..., as in a ... for the books, is a surprise result

explanation.surface: Someone shows up in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: appearing somewhere, and a surprising reversal in sport.

clue.text: Last recipient endures aggravation

indicators.note: aggravation means stirring up trouble, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: The final person to receive something puts up with annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the final consumer who actually receives and uses a product.

clue.text: Set a value on pie first having salt

indicators.note: first says the pie word comes before the valuing word

parts.note: a tart is a pie
to rate is to set a value on

explanation.surface: Pricing a pie that has been seasoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is the chemistry sense, a compound of an acid, not the table condiment; 'first' reverses the order the clue gives the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tartrate is a chemical salt of tartaric acid, as in cream of tartar.

clue.text: Metal can's contents can be found in the bathroom

definitions.text: can be found in the bathroom

indicators.note: contents says the letters are taken from inside the words metal can

explanation.surface: What is inside a tin turns up beside the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is kept in bathrooms for use after bathing.

clue.text: Flat race unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished says the word for race loses its final letter

parts.note: a race is an event at an athletics meeting

explanation.surface: A level track race that was never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and smooth, a synonym of flat.

clue.text: Front vehicle needs protector

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a guard is a protector

explanation.surface: The leading vehicle requires an escort.
explanation.definitionFit: The vanguard is the leading part of an army or movement, its front.

clue.text: One who has performed best as a defender

definitions.meaning: someone who ... a cause defends it

explanation.surface: A title holder seen as a protector.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the victor of a contest and an advocate standing up for a cause.

clue.text: Yarn Ellis spun

indicators.note: spun means twisted around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Ellis told a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' suggests a story; it is thread, and 'spun' rearranges ELLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton thread used for stockings.
